title: An independent evaluation finds that GraphCast and three other AI weather models matched the best operational cyclone track models in 2023
summary: Independent researchers at Colorado State University found that DeepMind's GraphCast and three other AI weather models matched the best operational models on 2023 cyclone tracks.
account: Google DeepMind's GraphCast was run live on the public charts of the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF) from 2023. DeepMind's blog of 14 November 2023 says that the live model predicted Hurricane Lee's landfall in Nova Scotia in September 2023 about nine days in advance. The blog says only “In September”, so the year is implied by its 14 November 2023 post date. ECMWF's newsletters 177 and 178, its science blog and its Severe Event Catalog do not document the case. MIT Technology Review quoted ECMWF's Peter Dueben: “It showed that these models are so good that we cannot avoid them anymore.” Researchers at CIRA, Colorado State University, who have no tie to DeepMind, applied the verification procedure of the National Hurricane Center (NHC) to cyclones from May to November 2023. They found that the track errors of GraphCast-operational and three other AI models were comparable to those of the best operational models, and adding all four improved the NHC track consensus by 11% at 120 h. NHC did not use the AI models in its 2023 operations. The evaluation appeared as a preprint on 8 September 2024 and after peer review in Artificial Intelligence for the Earth Systems on 20 October 2025, with the same 11% consensus gain at 120 h. The authors also found that the AI models' intensity forecasts had no skill against the simplest statistical models, because the models almost always weakened the storms. In its verification report of 30 March 2026, NHC states that the 2025 season marked the first time that it incorporated AI-based models into real-time operations. It reports that the Google DeepMind ensemble mean slightly outperformed NHC at lead times from 12 to 72 h.

fields.summary: Independent researchers at Colorado State University found that DeepMind's GraphCast and three other AI weather models matched the best operational models on 2023 cyclone tracks.
fields.account: Google DeepMind's GraphCast was run live on the public charts of the European Centre for Medium-Range Weather Forecasts (ECMWF) from 2023. DeepMind's blog of 14 November 2023 says that the live model predicted Hurricane Lee's landfall in Nova Scotia in September 2023 about nine days in advance. The blog says only “In September”, so the year is implied by its 14 November 2023 post date. ECMWF's newsletters 177 and 178, its science blog and its Severe Event Catalog do not document the case. MIT Technology Review quoted ECMWF's Peter Dueben: “It showed that these models are so good that we cannot avoid them anymore.” Researchers at CIRA, Colorado State University, who have no tie to DeepMind, applied the verification procedure of the National Hurricane Center (NHC) to cyclones from May to November 2023. They found that the track errors of GraphCast-operational and three other AI models were comparable to those of the best operational models, and adding all four improved the NHC track consensus by 11% at 120 h. NHC did not use the AI models in its 2023 operations. The evaluation appeared as a preprint on 8 September 2024 and after peer review in Artificial Intelligence for the Earth Systems on 20 October 2025, with the same 11% consensus gain at 120 h. The authors also found that the AI models' intensity forecasts had no skill against the simplest statistical models, because the models almost always weakened the storms. In its verification report of 30 March 2026, NHC states that the 2025 season marked the first time that it incorporated AI-based models into real-time operations. It reports that the Google DeepMind ensemble mean slightly outperformed NHC at lead times from 12 to 72 h.
